identification: Pair of English sterling silver fiddle pattern tablespoons, each with an engraved crest on the terminal. Full English hallmark row of four punches (lion passant, leopard's head, date letter, sovereign's head duty mark, so pre-1890 and probably London) plus maker's mark 'WE'. A London 'WE' on fiddle tablespoons is most likely William Eaton (prolific London spoonmaker, about 1813-1845), so probably late George III to early Victorian. Weight not stated; a pair of fiddle tablespoons is usually 120-150 g. Current bid A$60, estimate A$100-180.

viewing_check: Read the date letter and town mark with a loupe, confirm maker WE (William Eaton) and the duty head. Weigh the pair (expect 120-150 g). Look at bowl tips for wear/thinning and check the crest for a recognisable family.
